newsitem.title: FINLAND: Strong upturn for Finland's Merita Bank.
newsitem.headline: Strong upturn for Finland's Merita Bank.

text.p: Finland's biggest banking group Merita Oy on Wednesday reported sharply higher 1996 earnings, in line with expectations, and said it expected another clear improvement in operating earnings this year.

Reporting operating profit after credit losses up at 1.2 billion markka ($243 million) against 491 million in 1995, Merita proposed a 0.20 markka dividend per A share and a 1.60 markka payout per B share.
Both payouts were up from nothing last year, and were the first since the early 1990s from either of the banks which merged to form Merita in 1995 as Finland's banks were recovering from deep crisis.
The median of analysts' forecasts had been for a 1.27 billion markka operating profit after credit losses in a 1.1-2.5 billion markka range.
Merita said continued low interest rates and a steady improvement in its loan portfolio boded well for 1997.
"The Merita Group expects its operating result to improve clearly in the current year," Merita CEO Vesa Vainio said in a statement.

"This projection is based on the continued likelihood of low interest rates, which will reduce the group's funding costs, and the steady, albeit decelerating, downward trend in non-performing receivables and other underperforming assets.
"Other favourable developments include the decline in one-off integration expenses and the permanent cost benefits derived from the merger, the full impact of which is gradually being felt," it said.
Merita's banking arm Merita Bank's income-to-expenses ratio rose to 1.50 from 1.39.
Net loan and guarantee losses fell to 1.5 billion markka from 1.7 billion in 1995, with net income from financial operations up at 4.1 billion from 3.8 billion.
